snapshot_context: Steam catalogue snapshot, ~140k apps, dated approximately December 2024

app_universe.note: games.csv is the only table whose app_id is a verified 1:1 primary key covering the full catalogue. All other tables are subsets (categories, genres, tags) or near-total co-extensive sets (reviews, steamspy_insights) of this universe -- zero orphan app_ids were found in any table pointing outside games.csv.

files.read_recipe: read_csv(path, header=true, quote='"', escape='\\', sep=',', sample_size=-1) -- or read_csv_auto, which auto-detects escape='\\' correctly via its sniffer

columns.name: name
columns.note: 20 rows have literal '\N' as the name value -- true missing identifier, not a real null in the raw file

columns.name: release_date
columns.note: 28518/140082 rows (20.36%) are literal string '\N'; of the remaining 111564 castable dates, max date is 2024-10-28 -- no Nov/Dec 2024 rows despite the ~Dec-2024 snapshot date, i.e. right-truncated

columns.name: price_overview
columns.note: 63748/140082 (45.5%) are literal '\N'; of the 33661 is_free=1 rows, 33659 lack price_overview (expected); of the 106421 is_free=0 (paid) rows, 30089 (28.3%) ALSO lack price_overview -- pricing coverage on paid titles is materially incomplete. JSON values use backslash-escaped quotes (\") not doubled CSV quotes -- see hazards.

primary_key.evidence: count(*) = count(DISTINCT app_id) = 140082; zero full-row duplicates on all 7 columns

date_coverage.warning: 2024 total of 22022 is a 10-month figure (Jan-Oct only); treating it as a full year undercounts true 2024 releases and will misread as a YoY decline versus 2023's full-year 18217.

hazards: price_overview contains JSON with backslash-escaped quotes (\"), not doubled CSV quotes. A naive parser (Python csv.reader/pandas default, no escapechar) misaligns columns on 76334/140082 rows (54.49%). Extracting the 'type' column positionally (row[6]) after misalignment drops the correctly-identified game count from 122191 to 45857 -- a 62% loss that silently ejects well-known titles from any type=='game' filter. VERIFIED via direct row-by-row reproduction with Python's csv module. DuckDB's read_csv_auto sniffer auto-detects escape='\\' correctly on its own and needs no special handling; confirmed identical row counts and type distributions between naive auto-detect and explicit escape parsing.

'\N' is used as the null sentinel but is a literal 2-character string, not recognized as NULL by default CSV parsing, and cannot be combined with escape='\\' in DuckDB (mutually exclusive parser options) -- clean with NULLIF(col,'\N') then CAST, never trust default type inference on this file.
45.5% of rows are missing price_overview entirely, including 28.3% of nominally-paid (is_free=0) titles.
release_date is right-truncated at 2024-10-28 with zero Nov/Dec 2024 rows; 20.4% of all rows have no release_date at all.

primary_key.evidence: count(*) - count(DISTINCT (app_id,category)) = 0; app_id alone is NOT unique (avg 3.9 category-rows per app)

hazards: Long/tag table: joining on app_id alone fans rows out ~3.9x on average; use (app_id,category) or pre-aggregate before joining to games.csv.
Long/tag table: joining on app_id alone fans rows out ~2.9x on average.
12.58% of games.csv apps (17624 of 140082) have no genre row at all -- an inner join silently drops them.

Long/tag table: joining on app_id alone fans rows out ~14.8x on average (1744632 rows over 117505 apps) -- the single biggest fan-out risk in this dataset. 16.12% of games.csv apps (22577 of 140082) have no tag row at all.

hazards: All ten numeric-looking columns are typed VARCHAR by default because they contain literal '\N' sentinels -- NULLIF+CAST required, cannot combine nullstr='\N' with escape='\\' in DuckDB's read_csv (raises a Binder Error), so the fix must be applied post-read in SQL, not at read_csv time.

metacritic_score (96.6% null), recommendations (87.7% null), and steamspy_score_rank (99.96% null, essentially a dead column) are far too sparse to use as primary signals across the catalogue -- fine for spot-checks on AAA titles only.

review_score_description has 5 rows with literal '\N' alongside 19 real category labels including odd small-sample buckets like '1 user reviews' through '9 user reviews' that should be folded into a coarser bucket before any aggregation.

columns.name: owners_range
columns.note: 116582/140077 (83.2%) of ALL apps fall in the lowest bucket '0 .. 20,000' -- this column has almost no discriminating power above the bottom bucket and cannot support fine-grained owner-count analysis

columns.name: playtime_average_forever
columns.note: CONSTANT ZERO across all 140077 rows -- column carries no information

hazards: playtime_average_forever, playtime_average_2weeks, playtime_median_forever and playtime_median_2weeks are 0 for literally every one of 140077 rows. This is the single most consequential hazard for an Xbox/Game Pass investment analysis: engagement/playtime is the metric most relevant to a subscription business, and it is entirely absent from this dataset despite the columns existing and looking populated. Do not compute any engagement metric from this file; playtime is not observable here at all.
owners_range buckets 83.2% of the entire catalogue into a single lowest bin ('0..20,000') -- cannot distinguish a niche title from a mid-size hit within that bin.
developer/publisher missing for ~35% of apps -- studio-level rollups will undercount by roughly a third unless backfilled from another source.
5 rows in this file (140082 - 140077) exist in games.csv but have no steamspy_insights row at all.

hazards_summary_ranked: 1. price_overview (games.csv) and reviews (reviews.csv) contain JSON/HTML with backslash-escaped quotes (\"). A naive CSV parser without escapechar handling misaligns 76334/140082 games.csv rows (54.5%); positional extraction of 'type' after misalignment drops the correct game count from 122191 to 45857 (62% loss), silently dropping named indie titles from any type=='game' filter. DuckDB's read_csv_auto handles this correctly on its own -- verified.

2. steamspy_insights.csv's four playtime columns are a constant 0 for all 140077 rows -- there is no usable engagement/playtime signal anywhere in this dataset, which directly undercuts any Game Pass-relevant engagement analysis.

3. release_date is right-truncated at 2024-10-28 (zero Nov/Dec 2024 rows) and missing entirely ('\N') for 20.4% of all games -- any 2024 or recency-based trend must be caveated as a 10-month year and a ~1-in-5 unknown-date population.

4. The literal string '\N' is used as a null sentinel across five of six files and defeats default numeric type inference; it cannot be combined with escape='\\' in DuckDB's read_csv and must be cleaned with NULLIF+CAST after reading, file by file.

5. categories.csv/genres.csv/tags.csv are long tables (natural key = app_id+value, not app_id alone); naive joins on app_id fan out rows 3.9x / 2.9x / 14.8x respectively, and 4-16% of games have zero rows in each of these tables, so inner joins silently shrink the catalogue.
